question.text: For a linear plot of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>log</mi><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mfrac></mfenced></math> versus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>log</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></math> in a Freundlich adsorption isotherm, which of the following statements is correct? (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> are constants)

options.text: Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mfrac></math> appear in the slope term.

solution.text:
According to Freundlich isotherm,


xm=k.p1n   {Taking log}

log⁡xm=log⁡k+1nlog⁡P

y=c+mx (Straight line equation)

So, intercept is log k and slope is=1n.
